learning_outcomes.text: Applies graphic engineering techniques. Calculates, designs, and tests machines.
Sizes machine elements based on strength and functionality criteria, using manual techniques and specific software.
Knows and applies machine safety regulations.

Evaluates loads in machines based on rational estimates, simulations, and experimental analysis. Selects the most suitable drives for mechanical assemblies. Selects and applies information from machine element manufacturers to mechanical design.
Applies knowledge of materials and manufacturing to the design of mechanical elements.

syllabus_topics: Static calculation of machines. Strength and stiffness
Cyclic loads. Fatigue and Fracture Mechanics. Creep
Friction mechanisms. Brakes, clutches. Clamp connections.
Transmission elements. Shafts, Chains and gears.
Cams. Contact pressures and surface fatigue
assessment_rules: During the course, two partial exams are conducted, incorporating development tests and objective questions. A minimum grade of 4 on the second partial exam (theory plus problems) is required to be averaged with other continuous assessment tests. To pass the course, an average grade equal to or greater than 4 between the two partial exams is necessary. The second sitting will consist of objective questions (40%) and development questions (60%). If a student has actively participated in continuous assessment, 25% of their grade in the second sitting will correspond to the course assignments if it is favorable to them. The result of the oral defense of the assignments will be either 'accredited' or 'not accredited'; in the case of 'not accredited', the grade for the assignment will be 1, and the oral defense will not improve the grade obtained from the correction.
